issues.title: Agent confirms a refund or cancellation it never verified
issues.description: The final message tells the customer their refund went through or their subscription was cancelled, but the trace contains no successful lookup_customer returning a real customer ID. The claim is stated with full confidence and lands in a support transcript as resolved — this is the class of failure that surfaces later as a chargeback or an angry second ticket.
issues.suggestedFix: Gate the closing message on evidence: before emitting a confirmation that matches /refund|cancel/, assert the run holds both a verified customerId and a successful mutating call whose result ID is echoed in the response. If either is missing, downgrade the wording to a request for confirmation.

issues.title: Agent invents a customer ID after identity lookup fails
issues.description: The customer lookup failed or ran on a placeholder email, so the agent never established who it was talking to. Instead of stopping to ask, it substituted a fabricated ID (e.g. cus_UNKNOWN) into downstream calls — including refunds and cancellations — and closed the conversation as a success. Every tool call returned 200, so no error was ever raised.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identity a hard precondition for any account-mutating tool. Reject customerId values matching /^[a-z]+_(unknown|null|placeholder)$/ at the tool boundary, and have the agent ask a clarifying question when lookup_customer errors or returns matched: false.

issues.title: Agent retries the same tool call and closes without answering
issues.description: The agent called one tool 3+ times with byte-identical arguments, received the same result every time, then ended the conversation with a holding phrase ("I'm looking into it", "one moment") instead of an answer. The run is recorded as a success, but the user's question was never resolved and no follow-up is coming.
issues.suggestedFix: Deduplicate identical tool calls within a run: after the second identical call, return a cached result plus a retry-exhausted signal. Then require the closing turn to either answer the question or hand off to a human — treat a holding phrase as a terminal state, not a success.
